summary:
The Improving Federal Building Security Act of 2024, Pub. L. No. 118-157, establishes temporary requirements, codified as a note to 40 U.S.C. § 1315, governing Facility Security Committee responses to Federal Protective Service security recommendations for covered facilities.

Section 2(a) defines “agency” by reference to 5 U.S.C. § 551, “Secretary” as the Secretary of Homeland Security, and “Facility Security Committee” as a committee composed of representatives of all Federal tenants in a specific non-military facility, the facility security organization, and the owning or leasing Federal tenant, with responsibility for facility-specific security issues and approving implementation of security measures and practices.

Section 2(b) requires the head of a Facility Security Committee, or designee, not later than 90 days after the Federal Protective Service issues a facility-security recommendation, to respond to the Secretary indicating whether the Committee intends to adopt or reject the recommendation and describing the financial implications of adoption or rejection, including whether benefits outweigh costs. If the Committee intends to reject the recommendation, the response must include a justification for accepting the risk posed by rejection. The Secretary must develop a method to monitor recommendations and responses and take reasonable action to ensure Facility Security Committee responsiveness.

Section 2(c) requires the Secretary, not later than 270 days after enactment and annually thereafter, to submit to the Senate Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs and the House Committees on Homeland Security and Transportation and Infrastructure a report for the preceding fiscal year summarizing FPS recommendations, acceptance and rejection percentages, untimely response percentages, rejection justifications, financial implications, mitigation steps for rejected recommendations, and trends. Reports must be unclassified, with a classified annex permitted, and the Secretary must annually brief the same committees on the most recent report.

Section 2(d) requires, not later than 180 days after enactment, an unredacted report to the same committees on all surveillance technology recommended by FPS and any intended use of that technology. Section 2(e) provides that no additional funds are authorized to be appropriated to carry out the Act. Section 2(f) sunsets the Act five years after enactment and requires the Comptroller General, by the same five-year deadline, to report to Congress on the Act’s effectiveness. Section 2(g) limits application to General Services Administration facilities under FPS protection and non-GSA facilities that pay fees to FPS for protection.
